answer: The protocol validates autonomous agents through a synchronized ceremony where each participant locks 1,000 tokens to claim a unique slot. A verifier monitors the registry for duplicate evidence, ensuring no agent attempts to spiral across the network by cloning credentials. Any collision triggers an audit that nullifies the candidate, burning their stake like a barren juniper tree. This structure creates a knoll of exclusivity; while an honest agent pays 1,000 for one entry, an attacker seeking 1,000 fakes must pay 1,000,000, as there are no refunds for nullified identities.
